Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Call recap:
- Primary constraint: Aurora will be processing PHI and requires network isolation + customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Current state: teams are calling OpenAI endpoints today; some models live on a legacy GPU cluster (self-hosted) for high-throughput batch jobs.
- Goals: reduce per-token cost, maintain sub-200ms serving latency for lookup-style prompts, and meet compliance (audit logs, retention controls).

Options we discussed (high-level):
- Hosted API (fastest to deploy) — good for evaluation/non-PHI traffic.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) — predictable throughput, easier pilot for production traffic.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) — required for full PHI scope and when customer-managed KMS & air-gapped environment are needed.

Action items / next steps:

Hi all — thanks for the details. Quick technical read and recommended path below.

Short answer: pilot on Dedicated capacity, then migrate to Private VPC for full PHI scope.

Rationale and details:
- Dedicated capacity: supports reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and can be configured with VPC peering for log delivery. However, Dedicated does not currently support customer-managed KMS in the hosted control plane by default. We can provide an encrypted data path and audit logging to meet many compliance needs during pilot, but for true customer-managed keys and isolated control plane you’ll need Private.

- Private (VPC/on-prem): required when customer-managed KMS + air-gapped control plane are contractually mandated. Timeline for full Private deployment (production-grade): ~6–8 weeks from decision (includes provisioning, network peering, KMS integration, and acceptance testing).

Migration from legacy GPU cluster:
- Model artifacts: we can import model weights and tokenizer files. If they’re using custom kernels or unsupported ops, we’ll need a short portability runbook (2–3 days) to validate.
- Quantization: recommending int8/llm.int8 where feasible to reduce memory and cost; we’ll run an evaluation to check quality/regression on your prompt set.
- KV cache & batching: to hit sub-200ms for lookup prompts, we’ll configure aggressive prefix caching + small-batch async serving on Dedicated during the pilot.

Pilot recommendation (concrete):
1) Dedicated pilot — 2x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs, 6-week window. Objectives: validate latency, cost, and model parity against current cluster.
2) Security review during pilot — deliver audit logs, retention controls, and a SOC2 artifact bundle (we’ll provide SOC2 answers).
3) If pilot passes, move to Private VPC for PHI traffic only (migration plan & timeline: 6–8 weeks).

Blockers / risks:
- If models use proprietary CUDA kernels that are not supported in our runtime, we’ll need a short engineering effort (1–2 weeks) to either upstream kernels or provide a compatible runtime build.
- Customer-managed KMS adds ~1–2 weeks to the Private provisioning timeline depending on KMS vendor and key rotation policies.
